Toho CEO Reveals 'Godzilla Minus One' U.S. Success Was a Coincidence, Not a Master Plan

30 Oct 2026, 07:34 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Entertainment Desk · Source: variety.com

Image: Lin Ying-Hsuan — Creative Commons

Key takeawaysToho CEO Matsuoka Hiro revealed at the Tokyo International Film Festival that the blockbuster North American box-office run of "Godzilla Minus One" stemmed from opportunistic circumstances rather than a calculated corporate strategy. Speaking during an "Academy in Tokyo

Toho CEO Matsuoka Hiro revealed at the Tokyo International Film Festival that the blockbuster North American box-office run of "Godzilla Minus One" stemmed from opportunistic circumstances rather than a calculated corporate strategy. Speaking during an "Academy in Tokyo" panel alongside Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences CEO Bill Kramer, Matsuoka discussed how the kaiju film ultimately grossed $57.1 million in North America.

Unlocking the North American Market

Matsuoka explained that the successful rollout began after a U.S. trip where he spoke directly with film exhibitors. During these conversations, he learned that Hollywood studios were failing to produce enough films to satisfy audience demand. Exhibitors suggested that Toho should look into anime, which helped Matsuoka realize the extensive popularity of Japanese animation in the United States. Since Toho already owned the iconic "Godzilla" franchise, leadership decided to test the waters and distribute the film themselves.

The decision initially faced internal skepticism. Matsuoka noted that colleagues within Toho were deeply concerned about the proposed U.S. release because the company had previously struggled with international distribution. However, the film defied expectations, performed strongly at the box office, and ultimately returned its revenue directly to Toho.

"It was all a coincidence," Matsuoka told the audience regarding the unexpected opportunity. "It wasn't a strategy; we just tried."

Future Releases and Industry Insights

Following the unexpected triumph, Toho has mapped out future plans for the franchise. The upcoming follow-up from director Yamazaki Takashi, titled "Godzilla Minus Zero," is scheduled to open in Japan on Nov. 3 before arriving in North America on Nov. 6. Distribution in the U.S. will be handled by Gkids, the distributor that Toho acquired in 2024.

During the broader industry discussion, Matsuoka and Kramer touched on several key topics affecting global cinema:

  • Theatrical Exhibition vs. Streaming: Both executives agreed that cinemas and streaming platforms serve complementary roles rather than acting as adversaries. Matsuoka pointed out that Japanese cinemas successfully lured audiences back post-pandemic through repertory screenings, including retrospectives of Hayao Miyazaki's films.
  • Global Audiences: Kramer highlighted Bong Joon Ho's work and the success of films like "Parasite" as proof that global audiences have become increasingly open to subtitles and foreign-language cinema. He also noted that Asia remains an extremely vital region for the global film market, with 25% of the Academy's voting members currently based outside the United States.
  • Artificial Intelligence: Addressing technological shifts, Matsuoka characterized AI as a practical tool for maximizing workflow while emphasizing the need to monitor its impacts carefully. Kramer reaffirmed that the Academy remains dedicated to honoring human authorship and creation.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers and film enthusiasts looking to verify these statements can review the original coverage published by Variety. Because the remarks were delivered live at a public festival session, details regarding internal corporate discussions and future release windows are limited to what executives chose to disclose on stage.

  • What is confirmed: "Godzilla Minus One" grossed $57.1 million in North America; Toho acquired Gkids in 2024; "Godzilla Minus Zero" is slated for a Japanese release on Nov. 3 and a North American release on Nov. 6; and Toho's CEO explicitly stated the initial U.S. expansion was an experimental attempt rather than a mapped-out strategic campaign.
  • What remains unknown: Precise details regarding Toho's broader long-term international distribution budgets, specific terms of the Gkids integration, and the exact financial metrics of future franchise installments have not been fully detailed.

For complete context and direct reporting on the panel, readers can consult the official report on Variety at https://variety.com/2026/film/festivals/godzilla-minus-one-us-success-wasnt-strategy-toho-chief-1236933968/.
